findings.text: The IO header uses a define guard to ensure single inclusion within a translation unit.

The special register identifier AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_SPSR_EL1 corresponds to value 0xC200, while AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_ELR_EL1 corresponds to 0xC201, and AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_SP_EL0 corresponds to 0xC208, and AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_SPSEL corresponds to 0xC210, and AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_CURRENTEL corresponds to 0xC212, and AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_DAIF corresponds to 0xDA11, and AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_NZCV corresponds to 0xDA10, and AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_FPCR corresponds to 0xDA20, and AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_DSPSR_EL0 corresponds to 0xDA28, and AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_DLR_EL0 corresponds to 0xDA29.

The special register identifier AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_SPSR_EL2 corresponds to value 0xE200, while AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_ELR_EL2 corresponds to 0xE201, and AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_SP_EL1 corresponds to 0xE208, and AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_SPSR_INQ corresponds to 0xE218, and AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_SPSR_ABT corresponds to 0xE219, and AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_SPSR_UND corresponds to 0xE21A, and AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_SPSR_FIQ corresponds to 0xE21B, and AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_SPSR_EL3 corresponds to 0xF200, and AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_ELR_EL3 corresponds to 0xF201, and AARCH64_INSN_SPCLREG_SP_EL2 corresponds to 0xF210.

The system register identifier AARCH64_INSN_SYSREG_TPIDR_EL1 corresponds to value 0x4684, while AARCH64_INSN_SYSREG_TPIDR_EL2 corresponds to 0x6682, and AARCH64_INSN_SYSREG_SP_EL0 corresponds to 0x4208.

The condition identifier AARCH64_INSN_COND_EQ corresponds to 0x0 for equality, while AARCH64_INSN_COND_NE corresponds to 0x1 for inequality, and AARCH64_INSN_COND_CS corresponds to 0x2 for unsigned higher or same, and AARCH64_INSN_COND_CC corresponds to 0x3 for unsigned lower, and AARCH64_INSN_COND_MI corresponds to 0x4 for minus, and AARCH64_INSN_COND_PL corresponds to 0x5 for plus, and AARCH64_INSN_COND_VS corresponds to 0x6 for overflow, and AARCH64_INSN_COND_VC corresponds to 0x7 for no overflow, and AARCH64_INSN_COND_HI corresponds to 0x8 for unsigned higher, and AARCH64_INSN_COND_LS corresponds to 0x9 for unsigned lower or same, and AARCH64_INSN_COND_GE corresponds to 0xa for signed greater or equal, and AARCH64_INSN_COND_LT corresponds to 0xb for signed less, and AARCH64_INSN_COND_GT corresponds to 0xc for signed greater, and AARCH64_INSN_COND_LE corresponds to 0xd for signed less or equal, and AARCH64_INSN_COND_AL corresponds to 0xe for always.

The field position identifier A32_RN_OFFSET corresponds to 16 for the base register, while A32_RT_OFFSET corresponds to 12 for the first target, and A32_RT2_OFFSET corresponds to 0 for the second target.
The indicator arch_has_dev_port reports true for device port support, while IO_SPACE_LIMIT corresponds to PCI_IO_SIZE less one, and PCI_IOBASE corresponds to PCI_IO_START viewed as IO memory.

Decoded instructions are classified by width into 32 and 64 bit forms, by branch intent covering plain, linked, return and compare or test based variants, by access width across byte to doubleword, by load store shape covering register and immediate offsets plus pre and post indexed pairs and acquire release and exclusive flavours including signed variants, and by add subtract forms with optional flag update.

Further classification covers extension kinds for unsigned and signed byte half word and doubleword, move wide intents for zero keep and invert, bitfield moves including unsigned and signed flavours, byte reversal widths, divide and variable shift or rotate ops, multiply add or subtract triples, logical ops with optional flag setting including bic orn eon variants, prefetch kind level and retention policy, address formation kinds, atomic memory ops, ordering strengths, and barrier scopes from full system down to inner non and outer shareable with store load distinctions.

A helper template creates a pair for each named opcode: a matcher that checks a masked code against an expected value with a compile time guard that the value fits the mask, and a getter that returns the expected value. This yields uniform branch, barrier, load, store and hint testers.

A hint word is treated as steppable only after confirming hint class, then examining a masked subfield. The accepted set includes pointer authentication strip and sign variants, branch target identification flavours, and no operation, while all other hint subfields are rejected.

Branch recognition aggregates direct, linked, compare zero or nonzero, test bit set or clear, return including authenticated forms, indirect register jumps including authenticated forms, and conditional branches. An immediate only subset excludes register indirect and return forms, while address formation recognition groups the two PC relative forms.

Data synchronization recognition accepts either base or extended non sharable forms. General barrier recognition accepts data memory and data synchronization fences, instruction synchronization, speculation barrier, exclusive clear, and speculative store bypass fences including the privileged variant.

Single copy recognition groups immediate, pre indexed and post indexed forms separately for stores and loads, while pair recognition groups plain, pre indexed and post indexed pair forms. Literal use recognition covers PC relative loads including signed word form, PC relative address formation, and PC relative prefetch.

Hint construction combines a base hint encoding with a caller supplied operation field. No operation is produced as the hint with the NOP operation, and NOP detection compares a full word for equality with that generated value.
A callback type denotes a tester that accepts a full processor state word and returns a boolean decision, allowing callers to inject state dependent checks without exposing checker internals.

Width specific MMIO stores are provided for byte, halfword, word and doubleword. Each accepts a value and a volatile IO address and performs a single width matched store that also permits the zero register as a value source.

Width specific MMIO loads are provided for all four widths. Each load may be patched at boot between plain and strengthened sequences: an optional outer shareable barrier addresses one platform erratum, and an optional acquire form addresses device ordering, otherwise a plain load is used.

IO read ordering combines a DMA read barrier with a synthetic control dependency from the read value so later delay loops ordered by an instruction barrier in the cycle counter cannot migrate before the read. IO write ordering is a DMA write barrier, other directions are empty, and short aliases map read, write and full fences to those primitives.

Big endian IO helpers pair raw accesses with conversion and ordering: reads convert from big endian then apply the read fence, writes apply the write fence then convert to big endian before the raw store, for halfword, word and doubleword widths.

Aligned block stores for 32 and 64 bit elements accept only block counts of eight, four, two or one. Larger blocks use unrolled width matched stores at increasing element offsets, while a single element delegates to the corresponding raw store.

Passing any count other than eight, four, two or one to the aligned block helpers triggers a compile time failure rather than a runtime fallback, so callers must guarantee one of the supported sizes and suitable alignment.

The 32 and 64 bit IO copy wrappers select a fast path when the element count is a compile time constant in the supported set, issuing the matching unrolled helper followed by a guest hint, and otherwise delegate to a full copy routine that handles arbitrary counts.

Full IO copy routines for 32 and 64 bit elements are exported for arbitrary counts. Each forwards to a shared aligned copy engine with its element width and then issues a guest hint to complete the sequence.

Arbitrary length aligned copies progress from large to small chunks: first as many eight element blocks as fit, then an optional four block when at least four remain, then an optional two block when at least two remain, and finally an optional single when the total is odd, advancing both pointers after each stage.

User requested protection for IO mappings is validated for a user permission bit to reject none and execute only requests with a null result. Valid requests keep the kernel base mapping but replace only the attribute index field with the caller supplied index before delegating to the low level mapper.
A hook type allows confidential computing layers to intercept mapping protection, accepting a physical base, a byte length and a protection pointer and returning an integer status.

Protection values expose a reader for the raw integer and a modifier that clears a caller supplied mask from a base value then sets caller supplied bits, used to splice attribute fields without disturbing other flags.
Low level IO remapping is the central entry for creating device mappings from a physical base, length and protection, returning an IO cookie on success for use by the flavour wrappers.

Mapping creation fails with null when the end address escapes the physical mask, when the base lies in mapped RAM with a one time warning, or when a registered protection hook reports an error with a warning, preventing RAM aliasing and unapproved attributes.
Frame classification first discards bogus numbers whose physical round trip does not preserve identity, then consults the early reservation map to decide whether the frame counts as mappable memory.

The wrapper ioremap uses device non gather non reorder semantics, while ioremap_wc uses normal non cacheable semantics, and ioremap_np uses device non posted semantics, and ioremap_encrypted uses normal kernel semantics.

Cacheable remapping first tests whether the base lies in mapped memory and if so returns the existing linear alias directly, otherwise it creates a new normal cacheable mapping through the low level mapper.
Linear address translation subtracts the physical base offset and adds the kernel page offset to convert a physical address to its permanent kernel virtual alias.

Protected device queries report false outside realm execution and otherwise delegate to a realm service check over the requested byte range, allowing confidential guests to distinguish protected regions.
Presence macros advertise that valid physical range checking and RAM remap permission queries are implemented for this architecture.
Realm execution is detected through a rarely taken static branch tracking presence of the realm service interface, returning true only when that service is active.

Protection assessment aligns the requested interval outward to granule boundaries then repeatedly queries the IPA state service for the next homogeneous extent, advancing the cursor to each reported top until the end is reached or an empty extent appears.

Range checks treat address wrap as unprotected with a warning, abort the walk on query failure or non advancing extents with warnings, and report protected only when the full aligned interval completes without encountering an empty state.
